one_liner: CIA field officer who runs covert paramilitary and intelligence operations overseas in dangerous environments; built for former special operations or combat aviation veterans.
fit_summary: This posting has a hard minimum qualification of active-duty service in Special Operations, Combat Arms, or Aviation career fields, and nothing on file shows Daniel has military service. Daniel's emergency-management consulting, policy knowledge, and people skills are real strengths, but they do not substitute for the required military background. Unless Daniel has qualifying service not on file, Daniel should not apply here and should target other CIA or national-security roles instead.
eligibility: Required: prior active duty in the U.S. Armed Forces in Special Operations, Combat Arms, or Aviation/aviation-related specialties. This is a minimum qualification, not a preference.
Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution (or within one year of earning one); a 3.0+ GPA is preferred.
U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain a Top Secret/SCI clearance, including a background investigation and likely polygraph.
Must complete specialized paramilitary training, show a high level of physical readiness, and sign a 5-year Contract Term Agreement.
Open to the public, but the military requirement effectively limits it to veterans and service members.
strategy: First confirm honestly whether you have any qualifying active-duty service. If you don't, skip this posting, because applications without it will not pass screening.

Redirect to CIA Directorate of Operations roles with no military requirement, such as Operations Officer or Collection Management Officer, or to analyst roles. Your policy expertise and relationship-building skills fit those far better.
Also consider FEMA, DHS, and Virginia Department of Emergency Management positions, where IEM consulting experience maps directly onto the specialized experience.
For any CIA application, apply through cia.gov/careers and start early, because CIA processing and clearance can take a year or more.
Keep your resume to two pages and frame the IEM work around client-facing government projects, operational planning, and decision-making under time pressure, with dates and hours per week stated.
Do not post about the application publicly, and keep finances and history clean ahead of the background investigation.
resume_bullets: Supported [government client type] emergency management and disaster recovery programs at IEM as [title], coordinating [number] stakeholders across [agencies] to [specific outcome].
Prepared [briefings/plans/reports] on [preparedness or recovery topic] for [audience], translating policy requirements into actionable guidance under [deadline] timelines.
Built working relationships with [federal/state/local officials], resolving [issue type] and maintaining client satisfaction on [contract/project].
interview_questions: Describe a time you made a critical decision under time pressure with incomplete information.
How have you built trust quickly with someone whose goals differed from yours?
Tell us about leading a team or project in a stressful, high-stakes environment.
Why do you want to serve in the Directorate of Operations, and how do you handle extended overseas assignments?
watch_outs: The active-duty Special Operations, Combat Arms, or Aviation requirement is disqualifying without that service.
The role requires significant personal risk, rigorous physical standards, and most of a career spent overseas, under a 5-year contract.
The TS/SCI clearance and polygraph process is long and intrusive.
No telework is allowed, and schedules are erratic.
